chapter: Sam Morgan, repertoire and Silver Leaf
title: Blues, and hymns by brass bands
summary: Bands played blues without music, learned first because of few notes; only brass bands played hymns.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: Could, could Perez play blues? Did they play blues? Oh yeah, yeah. They wouldn't read when they played blues.
They didn't do all that, yeah. Did they use music when they played the blues too?
Well no, no, no, they didn't use the music for that.
They could just play that original blues.

Yeah, they just played the blues, yeah. And practically all bands would, what happened with that, all bands or orchestras would start, that was the first thing they learned. Yeah. Yeah. They played the blues, well, there wasn't much to do with the blues, you got a few notes to handle, and you know, you don't have many notes to pull with, a few notes. And that's why they all wanted the blues right away.
What about hymns? Did any other band play hymns?
Well no, I never heard them play hymns. Never heard them. They could have been playing, but I never heard any. But the brass bands did play hymns.
Brass bands, yeah, they played hymns.
